item.title: Inferring Transition-Dipoles from Two-Dimensional Infrared Spectroscopy with Deep Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.19972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy is a powerful nonlinear technique for probing vibrational couplings, anharmonicities, coherence, and molecular dynamics. Among the microscopic parameters encoded in 2D IR spectra, transition dipoles are fundamental quantities that characterize molecular structure and govern light-matter interactions. However, reconstructing these quantities from spectroscopic data remains a challenging inverse problem.
